subject: Private Offer: staggered billback & multi-SKU passback sequencing
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightlayer.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Sam Li <sam.li@brightlayer.com>
Cc: procure@brightlayer.com
Date: 2028-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private Offer: staggered billback across SKUs and channel passback sequencing

Hi Connor & team,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing the BrightLayer private offer and need clarity on how Redwood handles a staggered billback for a multi-SKU deal and how passbacks to our reseller network would be sequenced. High-level asks: 

- Can you provide an example invoice schedule for a 3-SKU bundle split across quarterly billbacks (Q1/Q2/Q3)?
- How do reseller/distributor passbacks map to the private offer? Is there a waterfall (reseller first, distributor holdback, then Redwood retention) and can you show the margin math?
- Any constraints on using a split-invoice approach vs. single invoice with crediting?

I've attached our PO specs and a simple proforma. We need a draft by EOD Thursday so procurement can incorporate into our SOW. If helpful, happy to jump on a call.

Attachments: BrightLayer_PO_Specs.pdf (proforma included)

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement, BrightLayer
M: +1-415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered billback across SKUs and channel passback sequencing

Hi Marta — thanks for the detail and the proforma. We'll put together three sample scenarios (steady-state, ramp, and early-churn) that show the invoice flow and the channel margin waterfall.

Ben (sales) and Irene (deal ops) are looped in — can you confirm the distributor name we should show on the passback lines? Also, do you expect taxes to be passed through to the reseller or handled upstream?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft passback/waterfall for BrightLayer (staggered billback)

Connor / Irene — rough proposal below that we can turn into the Excel proforma (attached). Naomi, tagging you because we'll need accounting confirmation on invoice timing and tax treatment.

Proposal (high level):
- Deal: 3 SKUs (Core Inference, Premium Support, Reserved Capacity) total list price = $1,200,000/year
- Payment cadence: private offer with staggered billback: 40% at contract execution (covers Core + Support), 30% at 90 days (reserved capacity start), 30% at 180 days (true-up / additional usage line)

Channel margin waterfall (example numbers):
- List price per SKU (example): Core $800k, Support $200k, Reserved $200k
- Reseller passback: 12% of list on Core & Reserved, 6% on Support (paid at each invoice event)
- Distributor holdback: 3% applied on second invoice (30-day escrow) returned after 90 days if no chargebacks
- Redwood retention: remainder after passbacks and holdbacks; show net rev and effective margin per SKU

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Option A (preferred): generate separate invoice lines per SKU at each milestone. This makes passback math explicit and easier for reseller invoicing.
- Option B: single invoice with credit memos to reflect the later-passback items — workable but increases bookkeeping for BrightLayer and reseller.

Attachments: proforma_worked_examples.xlsx (I built steady-state/ramp/churn tabs)

Next steps for external: ask BrightLayer which option they prefer (separate invoice per milestone vs single invoice + credits). Also confirm distributor legal name and whether reseller wants passback as percentage of list or a fixed per-seat fee.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightlayer.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Li <sam.li@brightlayer.com>, procure@brightlayer.com
Date: 2028-03-20T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered billback across SKUs and channel passback sequencing

Connor / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications before you finalize the examples: 

- We prefer Option A (separate invoice lines per milestone) for auditability.
- Distributor: AlderPoint Logistics, Inc. (exact legal name: AlderPoint Logistics, Inc.; tax ID to follow).
- Passback style: reseller wants percentage of list price for Core and Reserved; fixed fee for Support is OK but percentage is preferred if the math doesn't get messy.

Can you show three worked examples (numbers): steady state (no churn), aggressive ramp (50% usage growth across first 6 months), and early churn (20% reduction at month 4) — with clear per-invoice passback lines and net revenue to BrightLayer and to the reseller.

Also once the numbers are agreed, please send a DocuSign-ready term sheet — we plan to include it as an exhibit to our SOW.

Thanks,
Marta
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered billback across SKUs and channel passback sequencing

Hi Marta — attached is a short package: 1) worked proforma (steady-state / ramp / early-churn tabs) 2) annotated invoice examples (plain text CSV in the workbook) and 3) a redwood_private_offer_draft_v2.pdf term sheet. Key callouts below.

Quick summary of the three examples (numbers are rounded):
- Steady-state:
  * Invoice 1 (execution): Core $320k, Support $80k, Reserved $80k -> Reseller passback = 12% on Core ($38,400) + 6% on Support ($4,800) + 12% on Reserved ($9,600) -> BrightLayer net = remainder after passbacks/holding.
  * Invoice 2 (90d): Core $240k, Reserved $120k (holdback 3% on Reserved $6,000 held for 90d)
  * Invoice 3 (180d): Core $240k, Reserved true-up $0 (example) -> holdback released if no chargebacks.
- Ramp scenario: same sequencing, but Core usage scales so passback amounts scale; proforma shows per-invoice delta and cumulative reseller margin.
- Early churn: invoice 3 reduced by 20% on Core; proforma shows recovered holdbacks vs. required credits to reseller and net impact to BrightLayer.

Implementation recommendation: separate invoice lines per milestone (Option A). This makes visible the passback amounts to resellers and keeps holdbacks isolated to the specific SKU/invoice.

Next steps:
- Marta: confirm AlderPoint legal / tax id and whether BrightLayer wants holdback released automatically at day 90 or require a manual confirmation trigger.
- Once you confirm, we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready term sheet and route it to your procurement contact. HubSpot deal link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/BL-2028-0421

Attachments: redwood_private_offer_draft_v2.pdf (term sheet), proforma_passback.xlsx (worked examples)

Looking forward to the sync — I can set up 30 minutes tomorrow if that works for your schedule.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
